<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"a86bed3aa065fbfdc70f0994bd73eb73394f3143cd94e571e3d7cda1dca6961a"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported video ad and the leftover banner background do not appear on ootrandomizer.com when the reporter's own filter lists are applied:⁠ the Raptive/AdThrive loader is blocked, the ad slots render empty at zero size, and full-page vision found neither annotated target. Recommend closing as not reproduced; the only ad-recovery path on the page (html-load.com) is already neutralized because Base filter redirects the detection probe to noopjs.

## Policy rationale

The reported ads are served by a third-party ad network (Raptive/AdThrive), not the site's own advertising, so the first-party-ads policy does not apply. The report is not a paywall and not a German anti-adblock wall, and the page shows no anti-adblock message, so none of the no-rule policy clauses closes it. No policy clause blocks rule generation; the close is recommended on non-reproduction of the reported defect on the loaded page with the reporter's filter set.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43660752570

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `04e0f73`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

The domain-scoped cosmetic rule fluxpayroll.ai#⁠#⁠body ⁠> div.MuiPaper-elevation6 hides that one element and was verified in the reporter filter profile with the page intact and no residue. ## Rule `fluxpayroll.ai##body > div.MuiPaper-elevation6` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported symptom is a cookie-consent notice, not first-party advertising, a paywall, or a German anti-adblock wall, so none of the instruction's close rules applies. The page shows no anti-adblock gate and the captured requests contain no detector script, so no anti-adblock exemption or hand-off applies. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

### Issue URL (Anti Adblock Script) [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/faa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cbsnews.com%2Fnews%2Ffaa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know%2F) ### Comment > ### Issue Description > Anti-adblock wall on `cbsnews.com` via Admiral First-Party Proxy. > > * **A/B Test Behavior:** Clean/Incognito sessions are served an inescapable hard wall with no dismiss link and page scrolling locked (`overflow: hidden`). Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.gumtree.com the reported blank ad area is the empty top-takeover placement `#top_takeover-container` (271px tall, full width) left unfilled because gpt/prebid/adnami are blocked, and hiding it with `gumtree.com###top_takeover-container` removed the gap in the validated reporter-profile experiment (page integrity intact, no remaining blank ad area). The reporter's cookie-notice remark was not reproducible and belongs to the Cookie Notices filter. ## Rule `gumtree.com###top_takeover-container` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported defect is an empty ad container left by a blocked third-party ad (gpt/prebid/adnami), not the site's own advertising, so the 'first-party ads:⁠ no rule' policy line does not apply. Not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall (no detector script and no block message found), so the anti-adblock policy lines do not apply. German anti-adblock rule does not apply:⁠ the site is gumtree.com (UK), the page is in English, and no ad-block detection message is shown. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 7367](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L7367). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — watch.plex.tv leaves an empty Playwire display-ad slot that paints a blank dark-gray 728x114 rectangle between the hero carousel and the "What's On Now" section — the reporter's screenshot, still present with the reporter's own filter settings. The verified domain-scoped rule `watch.plex.tv##div[class^="DisplayAd-module__"][class*="inlineLeaderboard"]` removes it, with no remaining instances and an intact page. ## Rule `watch.plex.tv##div[class^="DisplayAd-module__"][class*="inlineLeaderboard"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported defect is a leftover third-party (Playwire) display-ad slot on watch.plex.tv, not the site's own first-party advertising, so the filter policy's first-party-ad exception does not apply. No paywall and no anti-adblock wall are involved; the page shows ordinary content with no detector message. The run instruction states no rule that closes this report, so rule generation is allowed. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 12431](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L12431). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — oggi.it leaves its ad slots unfilled, so they render as light-grey '.bck-adv' placeholder boxes labelled 'Pubblicità' (right rail beside the 'Racconto di una notte' article and between content rows); the repository already hides that same RCS ad wrapper on sister sites with `corriere.it,gazzetta.it##.bck-adv`, so the fix is adding oggi.it to that shared rule. The extension run proved `.bck-adv` goes visible→hidden, but the vision review refused to call the symptom resolved because the page's own blank rail column, column divider and lazily unloaded image bands remain, so the rule is filed unverified for human review.

## Candidate for review

`oggi.it,corriere.it,gazzetta.it##.bck-adv`

BaseFilter/sections/foreign.txt

Not verified: apply_rule did not reject the rule:⁠ on the reporter profile the DOM probe reported `.bck-adv` visible in phase B and hidden in phase C, and re-inspection of the phase-C tile shows the 'Pubblicità' panel gone from the rail. But environmentExperiment came back inconclusive and the vision review rejected:⁠ adLayoutResidue present, symptom not_resolved and non-empty remainingInstances — the blank right-rail column, the page's own thin vertical column divider and \~2900px of off-white lazily-unloaded bands lower down the page, gaps its own settlement section records as unchanged_before. The broader retry was rejected the same way, with a pageIntegrity 'regression' that is the pre-existing row of unloaded article thumbnails. Validated as the domain-scoped `oggi.it##.bck-adv`; the host merges the domain into the existing `corriere.it,gazzetta.it##.bck-adv` line when it builds the patch.

## Still visible after the rule

- Right-hand rail beside the 'Racconto di una notte' article — Tall empty reserved advertising rail to the right of the article, delineated by a thin vertical divider. No ad creative or 'Pubblicità' label is visible; the ad content is still absent, whether the placeholder was hidden by the candidate or failed to load.
- above SENZA WILLIAM / George torna a Eton e Kate Middleton, in tailleur, torna al lavoro con nuovo impegno per i neonati — Large empty white reserved advertising gap spanning the left content column above the 'SENZA WILLIAM' article and below the preceding content row; no ad creative or label is visible, leaving an oversized blank slot.
- LOVE STORY / Laura Torrisi, dopo Pieraccioni arriva il banchiere:⁠ chi è Giacomo Bolognini, l'amore «inaspettato» / LE DOMANDE DI OGGI — Large empty white reserved advertising gap in the right rail between the 'LOVE STORY' item and the 'LE DOMANDE DI OGGI' item; no ad creative, label, frame, or placeholder block is visible.
- Below the 'Novità / Iniziative / Oggi Consiglia' row, spanning the main column and right rail — Large reserved blank advertising area beginning immediately below the three navigation boxes and continuing downward. No ad creative or 'Pubblicità' label appears; the visible column divider runs through the reserved space, so this is the residual ad footprint the reporter described.
- Right-hand rail/main-column blank continuation from the navigation row — Continuation of the same large reserved blank ad area:⁠ the tile is empty white with only the vertical column divider visible. No ad creative or 'Pubblicità' label is present, so the reporter's ad-placeholder symptom remains as reserved blank space.
- and 13 more of the same, in the run artifacts

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's annotated area on minkara.carview.co.jp/smart/ is an emptied header ad wrapper (div.cen.banner) that still reserves a 51px blank band because the site's ad loaders are already blocked by published rules. Adding minkara.carview.co.jp#⁠#⁠.cen.banner hides that leftover; the A/B/C experiment and visual review verified the gap is gone with page integrity intact. ## Rule `minkara.carview.co.jp##.cen.banner` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is not the site's own advertising being deliberately blocked:⁠ the annotated region is an empty ad wrapper left behind after the site's own ad loaders (adcommon.js, microad, impact-ad) were already blocked by published rules, so hiding the leftover repairs filtering rather than targeting first-party ads. Not a paywall and not a German anti-adblock wall; the page shows no anti-adblock message and no detector script (get_applied_rules shows no anti-adblock rule acting, console/network show no wall). The repository policy's ad-blocking limitations do not apply:⁠ nothing here is a content-access gate, tracker, widget or social element. ## Place in the list [MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 2992](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/04e0f73b214ddc9d9c59ded9a5934878059d9f39/MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt#L2992). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On aptera.us/events/ a first-party theme script shows a delayed newsletter sign-up modal that also locks page scrolling (body.no-scroll), so the correct fix is a network rule blocking `||aptera.us/wp-content/themes/buddyboss-theme-child/assets/js/theme/newsletter-popup.min.js` rather than element hiding. The A/B experiment removed the pop-up and left the page scrollable with no residue, but the vision review stayed inconclusive (page integrity unclear for a network block), so the rule is handed to a maintainer for review.

## Candidate for review

`||aptera.us/wp-content/themes/buddyboss-theme-child/assets/js/theme/newsletter-popup.min.js`

AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule's environmentExperiment came back 'inconclusive' although it did not reject the rule:⁠ phase B showed the reported modal (.newsletter-popup--show visible over the dimmed Events page, body.no-scroll scroll lock) and phase C reported the rule 'applied' with the element not_found, document height back to 1921 and no occluded content. The vision review returned verdict 'inconclusive' with symptom 'resolved', adLayoutResidue 'absent', remainingInstances empty, observedDamage empty, but pageIntegrity 'unclear' because it is a network block whose effect on first-party interactive controls cannot be judged from static screenshots; failedCandidateChecks were empty. Element hiding of .newsletter-popup was deliberately not proposed:⁠ with the modal hidden the body.no-scroll lock (overflow:⁠hidden; position:⁠fixed; height:⁠100vh) stays and the close control is gone, leaving the page unscrollable.

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The store home page loads normally through the AdGuard CLI baseline, and neither the reporter-marked band (the "Новинки" section header, its own store banner, product cards) nor the rest of the page contains any third-party advertising, ad SDK or empty ad container. Nothing to filter, so the report can be closed as not reproduced.

## Policy rationale

No repository policy rule blocks rule generation for this report:⁠ it is not first-party advertising, a paywall, a German anti-adblock wall, another anti-adblock wall, or a scam page as far as the live evidence shows; the page simply shows no advertising to act on. The policy's first-party-advertising exclusion would additionally apply to the only promotional material actually present (the club's own shop banners and sponsor logos), but it is not the deciding rule here because no third-party advertising was reproduced either.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"2251bb9c4fd688f156b9a8f19fee254dc2bb30819007dd32385a3c7223262eab"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The "Please allow ads on this site" wall on index.hr did not reproduce:⁠ three loads of the reported page plus the experiment's unfiltered and filtered phases all showed the normal homepage with page integrity intact, while the page's Ad-Shield recovery platform (lava.perfectalto.com, detector ads.js, localStorage "cache_is_blocking_ads":⁠"true") is clearly active and already covered by the shared Ad-Shield scriptlets for index.hr. A host-block candidate was rejected because the vendor fell back to a new domain family (content-loader.com), so I recommend closing as not reproduced, with a maintainer re-check on iOS since that engine was not exercised here.

## Policy rationale

No repository policy rule closes this report:⁠ www⁠.index.hr is not a German site, the screenshot shows a non-German anti-adblock interstitial, and the run instruction's filter policy only withholds rule generation for anti-adblock walls whose detector script is missing from the captured requests. The captured requests do contain the detector:⁠ the first-party https:⁠//www⁠.index.hr/Scripts/adblockDetect/ads.js (200) and the third-party recovery protocol on lava.perfectalto.com / *.stg.lava.perfectalto.com (artifact:⁠har:⁠66ea6c83-2874-4e16-9d81-6f747cab17c5). Rule generation was therefore permitted; it failed on reproduction and on candidate rejection, not on policy.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.samsunhaber.com a fixed black cookie-consent bar (div.js-cookie-consent.cookie-consent) stays pinned over the mobile news feed because the page's own script writes display:⁠block!important inline, so the Cookie Notices filter's generic hiding rule has no effect. The domain-scoped CSS rule that moves and hides that element validated in the before/after experiment (banner hidden, page integrity intact, no residue), and the host will merge samsunhaber.com into the existing shared rule in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt. ## Rule `samsunhaber.com#$#.js-cookie-consent { position: absolute !important; left: -9999px !important; visibility: hidden !important; }` ## Policy rationale None of the run instruction's closing rules applies:⁠ this is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, not any anti-adblock wall (no detector involved) and not a scam/malware page. The reported element is a cookie notice, the declared subject of the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter ('designed to block both cookie notices and requests from cookie management platforms'). The filter policy prefers hiding over granting consent ('Whenever possible, non-essential cookies are declined by default'); the proposed rule only hides the bar and sets no cookie. The maintainer rules direct extending an existing shared rule with the reported domain instead of writing a duplicate line, and the target expression is such a shared rule, not a project-grouped one. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a316534364ae506f974ae6ec4595e238f5e9aaba/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 1176](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a316534364ae506f974ae6ec4595e238f5e9aaba/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L1176). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On blog.google the social share links are already filtered, but the share widget wrapper stays behind:⁠ the circular share button in the byline row remains and its popup is an empty white rounded box over the intro paragraph. Hiding `.uni-share-dropdown` alongside the existing `.uni-social-share` selector was verified in the locked CLI baseline — leftover gone, page intact, no remaining instances. ## Rule `blog.google##.uni-share-dropdown, .uni-social-share` ## Policy rationale The reported elements are a social share widget leftover and a newsletter subscription prompt, not first-party advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the instruction's close-or-hand-off rules applies. The share leftover is served in the page markup with no detector script among the captured requests, and the candidate is an element-hiding rule for a domain the Social filter already targets. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5a8cf08bf9df325c86faebf008fc1f32c450233e/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 4956](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/5a8cf08bf9df325c86faebf008fc1f32c450233e/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L4956). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"232bde0f5b1d459d2a0b4cea2e9cc03e0b350af7a3af7f4461cc1cd5e854c9fb"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reported annoyance on korben.info is the site's own promotion — a rotating in-house promo bar and in-article panel carrying the owner's Kassis app creative and a Patreon support ask, served entirely from korben.info's own HTML with no third-party ad request in the captured traffic. Because it is the site's own first-party advertising, the run instruction's policy gives it no rule, so the report is recommended for closing by a maintainer.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reported elements are the site owner's own promotion, so this rule blocks the fix. The instruction also states "The agent never closes an issue… a maintainer checks it and decides" — this outcome is the recommendation for that maintainer decision, not a closure. Evidence that the promotion is first-party:⁠ the promo is site-authored markup on korben.info (div.voxdrop-banner__inner.platform-promo-bar and div.patreon-support-banner) carrying its own data-kassis-* creative attributes, the Kassis icon is self-hosted at /img/v/kassis/, and korben.info's own /en/now/ page calls Kassis "my voice recognition software… finally available on the App Store" — i.e. the site owner's product, plus a Patreon membership appeal by the same owner. get_network_log for the reported page lists 55 requests, all first-party korben.info (plus the proxy's own local.adguard.org), with blockedCount 0 and no advertising host:⁠ there is no third-party ad or promo request to block. Noted for the maintainer, not applied here:⁠ the repository's Annoyances documentation lists "Block self-promotion of websites… if it is considered an annoying element" (Other Annoyances) and app-install banners (Mobile App Banners, whose header/menu exception applies to the 48px top bar), decisions made rule-by-rule by filter developers; the instruction's first-party rule takes precedence in this run.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43700477624

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — webseriessex.com's theme injects an in-player ad about 5 s into playback ("SKIP" / "Skip ad in N", filled by JuicyAds/Clickadilla) and pauses the video there; blocking the ad loaders does not stop it. Disabling the theme's own in-video ad flag with a domain-scoped set-constant scriptlet removes the overlay and lets the video play through, verified by apply_rule (before:⁠ paused at 5.2 s with SKIP; after:⁠ playing at 19.4 s, ad container absent, page intact). ## Rule `webseriessex.com#%#//scriptlet('set-constant', 'vidorev_jav_plugin_video_ads_object.vid_ads_m_video_ads', 'no')` ## Policy rationale No rule of the run instruction's filter policy closes this report:⁠ the ad is third-party ad-network advertising (JuicyAds poweredby.jads.co, Clickadilla bartererfaxtingling.com) filling the site's player slot, not the site's own self-promotional advertising. It is not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not any anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page never asks the visitor to disable the blocker; the failure is an in-player ad that stops playback. No policy restriction on the resource applies:⁠ the theme's own in-video ad flag is neutralized with a domain-scoped scriptlet, while the shared video-player SDKs the page also calls (imasdk, adsbygoogle) are left untouched. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/general_extensions.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/2614d31c30f970e50b8c1b7c90eb7261e76a9a55/BaseFilter/sections/general_extensions.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

### Issue URL (Anti Adblock Script) [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/faa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cbsnews.com%2Fnews%2Ffaa-ground-stop-canceled-flights-travelers-what-we-know%2F) ### Comment > ### Issue Description > Anti-adblock wall on `cbsnews.com` via Admiral First-Party Proxy. > > * **A/B Test Behavior:** Clean/Incognito sessions are served an inescapable hard wall with no dismiss link and page scrolling locked (`overflow: hidden`). Some regular sessions occasionally receive a variant with a delayed *"I'll fix it next time"* dismiss button. > * **Consent Requirement:** Only triggers after OneTrust (`cbsoptanon`) allows targeting/advertising cookies (`cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`). > > ### Proxied Admiral Script URLs Observed > * `https://silkyslumber.com/static/kmxtcpfvq/q1zxupa.js` > * `https://topicspin.com/static/k6vi91qgp/siqqoqasp4mu874ckh6569s5n2uum.js` > > ### Inline Bootstrap & Obfuscation Details > * Admiral's inline loader is wrapped in `loadAdmiralScript()` and invoked asynchronously inside `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` $\rightarrow$ `cmp.ot.targetingAllowed`. > * Because `loadAdmiralScript()` runs asynchronously after `document.currentScript` is `null`, inline scriptlets hooking `document.createElement` do not catch it. > * Evades generic Admiral signatures by aliasing `decodeURI` (`D(D(Y))`) and double-encoding `'admiral'` (`%25%36%31%64m%25%36%39%25%37%32%2561%6C`). > * Static Admiral Property ID in inline script: `QS01RDlDQzI1QTgyQ0FFMzUwNTQ5RkMwQUMtMg` > > ### Suggested / Verified Fix > Aborting synchronously when `loadAdmiralScript` is registered with `cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady` blocks Admiral before any proxied scripts are fetched: > ```adblock > cbsnews.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'cbsoptanon.onScriptsReady', 'loadAdmiralScript') > ``` ``` Username: @SpoiledSneeze ``` ### Screenshots

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The Winline popup overlay and cdek.shopping card from the reporter's screenshot never appeared on the reported sportsdzen.ru story in three unfiltered control loads (desktop) and one mobile load, where the page only served different rotating ads (myTarget/ad.mail.ru top banner, Yandex Direct cards); with the reporter's filter selection loaded no advertising was visible at all. No selector or request for the reported creatives could be observed, so no rule is proposed and the report can be closed as not reproduced.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

No rule of the run instruction's filter policy closes this report:⁠ the creatives on the page are served by third-party ad servers (ad.mail.ru, yandex.ru/ads), not the site's own first-party advertising; there is no paywall, no German anti-adblock wall, no other anti-adblock wall, and no scam/phishing content. Rule generation was allowed for this report, but no rule is proposed because the reporter-defined advertising creatives never rendered in any session, so no selector or request could be observed, authored or validated.

The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

m.facebook.com redirects logged-out visitors from the reported page to its login flow (/Boomsushi2022/ 302 -⁠> /login/ 302 -⁠> /unified/login_via/app/), so the "unclosable window" is Facebook's own login/registration gate and no page content exists behind it to unlock. Because content access measures are not blocked by ad filters and hiding the gate would only remove the user's only signal, no filter rule is appropriate and the report should be recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

Repository filter policy (limitations and exceptions):⁠ 'Content access measures like paywalls are not blocked by Ad blocking filters. However, they may be blocked by Tracking protection filters if their operation results in a violation of user privacy.' The reported overlay is Facebook's own login/registration requirement for viewing a page, a content access measure, not an ad and not an ad-blocker detector. Run instruction filter policy:⁠ 'Paywalls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing.' No other stated close rule applies (not the site's own advertising, not a German anti-adblock wall, and no ad-block detector script appears in the captured requests), so the report says no rule is needed. Run candidate rule policy:⁠ an overlay that gates content behind an action must not be hidden — 'Never hide the placeholder:⁠ that removes the user's only signal, leaves the function broken'. Here the gated function cannot be restored at all:⁠ logged-out requests for the reported page are answered with a redirect to the login flow, so no content exists behind the gate to unlock. No captured request shows an ad-blocker detector, and no third-party vendor script produces the gate, so no network or scriptlet rule has a causal target to neutralize.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's bottom-right cookie notice on myospots-int.com is the site builder's `.widget-cookie-banner` widget, and the repository already keeps that selector as a shared multi-domain rule, so myospots-int.com should be added to it. The scoped candidate was verified in the reporter-profile session:⁠ the panel was visible before and gone after, page integrity intact, no remaining instances. ## Rule `myospots-int.com##.widget-cookie-banner` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction closes only first-party ads, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls; a cookie-consent notice is none of them. Cookie notices are the stated subject of the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter (CONTRIBUTING), so this report is open to rule generation and the rule belongs in the Cookies section. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/40b2d6c8e5a3a7713e8a2e71936c24009039a855/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 11640](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/40b2d6c8e5a3a7713e8a2e71936c24009039a855/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L11640). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — newsroom.rolex.com serves its cookie-consent overlay from the third-party InMobi CMP (cmp.inmobi.com); the banner did not render for this egress, but blocking cmp.inmobi.com for this site verified in phase C (1/1 blocked) with an unchanged page, so newsroom.rolex.com is added to the repository's existing shared InMobi CMP rule. ## Rule `||cmp.inmobi.com^$domain=newsroom.rolex.com` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's close list covers first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, and anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script; a third-party cookie-consent notice is none of these. The symptom is produced by a loadable third-party CMP script visible in the captured request inventory (cmp.inmobi.com), which the guidance says to stop with a network rule, and the repository already keeps a shared rule family for exactly this host. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/9a9e090ed27c49dbfe3ab7b675a4b96ce4f1d4db/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 114](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/9a9e090ed27c49dbfe3ab7b675a4b96ce4f1d4db/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L114). ## Missing information - Full text of the shared `||cmp.inmobi.com^$domain=…` rule is not retrievable in bounded slices: The maintainer guidance tells me to add the reported domain to the existing shared rule instead of writing a new one. The matching rule is `||cmp.inmobi.com^$domain=<~400 domains>` at AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt line 114 (section "Cookies - Popular rules"). `search_rules` (domain inmobi.com, artifact d9b6e751-007b-49f4-80ff-fbf9dcd150c6) exposes it, but `get_detail` with key `matches.18.rule` truncates at \~8,000 of its 10,182 bytes ("...|musicstax.com|l"), and no other tool returns the rule text, so the exact extended rule cannot be written verbatim without inventing the unknown tail of the domain list. The proposal therefore names the reported-domain addition `||cmp.inmobi.com^$domain=newsroom.rolex.com` and relies on the host adding `newsroom.rolex.com` to that shared rule in the same file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Maintainer rules allow working with shared families where one fits; no shared family matches this class, so a new site-scoped element-hiding rule is written instead of a duplicate. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/9a9e090ed27c49dbfe3ab7b675a4b96ce4f1d4db/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On foxsports.com both reported leftovers reproduce:⁠ an inline "FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTER" signup card and a share block whose icons the Social filter already hides, leaving a "SHARE" heading over an empty row; a combined element-hiding rule hid both with page integrity intact, but the vision review still rejected it because a blank band between the reaction widget and the section divider remains, and measurement shows that band is the page's own padding and margins, which only a disallowed CSS injection could collapse.

## Still visible after the rule

- Below the “What did you think of this story?” reaction widget and above the divider/FIFA WORLD CUP MEN TRENDING section — A wide empty area follows the reaction widget; no SHARE heading, share icons, or share controls are visible before the divider and trending section, matching the reporter's empty share-row symptom.

## Missing information

- No placement guidance for a symptom family that spans two filters under the one-rule outcome limit: Issue #⁠247291's reporter-defined symptom family contains two distinct widget kinds:⁠ an inline newsletter/subscription signup card (Annoyances subscriptions, cf. the existing `foxsports.com#?#.tune-in-list > li.tune-in-item:has(... Newsletter)` rule in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) and a social share row (SocialFilter, cf. `~stylebook.de##.facebook-share` in SocialFilter/sections/general_elemhide.txt, which already empties the row). The run instruction says only the outcome may carry exactly one filter rule, and that placement is not declared, so a rule that must cover both instances (the apply_rule vision review treats both as one symptom family and rejects a candidate that fixes only one) has no stated file:⁠ no documented convention exists for a mixed-kind cosmetic rule whose selectors belong to two different filters.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — toolkit.fondazionescuola.it shows an iubenda Cookie Solution consent dialog ("INFORMATIVA", "Scopri di più e personalizza", "Accetta") fixed over the SCHOOL TOOLKIT header even with AdGuard Cookie Notices enabled. Extending the existing shared rule `||cs.iubenda.com^$domain=…` with this domain removed the dialog in the verified experiment without any observed damage. ## Rule `||cs.iubenda.com^$domain=toolkit.fondazionescuola.it` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall:⁠ the reported element is a third-party iubenda cookie-consent notice, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to handle. Not an anti-adblock wall at all, so the anti-adblock gate (detector script required) does not apply. Fits the filter policy for cookie notices:⁠ blocking the CMP's config request prevents the notice without needing an alternative consent mechanism on this page (no consent-gated iframes or embeds were found). Low-traffic considerations:⁠ the policy asks that low-traffic sites still be checked for third-party networks — here the offending resource is iubenda's third-party CMP, and the fix extends an existing shared iubenda rule rather than adding a site-specific workaround. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3b7ce90a9f581da50208330bd4750214849be8f8/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 294](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3b7ce90a9f581da50208330bd4750214849be8f8/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L294). ## Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"6774c4c57552876145fe3673080453b15bc1bc75674b4f3655150c7cb026b588"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

Environment:⁠ browser_extension (locked), pinned AdGuard Browser Extension v5.5.2.3, session launched with the reporter settings import (reported_on_current:⁠ AdGuard Base, French, URL Tracking; Stealth on). Live session:⁠ open_page on https:⁠//open.spotify.com/collection/tracks returned 200 but the URL redirected to https:⁠//open.spotify.com/ — the library page is login-gated and signing in is refused as an unsafe control, so the logged-out home page is what the session could load. Complete full-page vision of that page (capture 3cad6a79…, tiles 90aa6d9d…/23dbe0e3…/031a9028…, coverageComplete true) reports reporterSymptomPresence "absent", instanceCount 0:⁠ no ad banner, no in-player 'Publicité' panel and no reserved blank ad slot; the only ad-related text is the sidebar link "À propos des pubs" and Spotify's own "S'inscrire gratuitement" strip. inspect_ad_slots returned 0 candidate slots. Network (artifact:⁠har:⁠e1a06f4e-8245-4411-b495-7d40c918b7de, 175 requests, blockedCount 0) shows the site's ad serving is first-party:⁠ open.spotifycdn.com/cdn/build/web-player/home-ads-container.e4a7af91.js and .a499c441.css, spclient.wg.spotify.com/ads-identity-web-enricher/v1/gpcSignals, guc3-spclient.spotify.com/gabo-receiver-service event endpoints; no third-party ad-network host for the in-player ad appears. get_applied_rules shows the published baseline already neutralises Spotify's ad media on this exact URL:⁠ ||spotifycdn.com/audio/$media,\~xmlhttprequest,redirect=noopmp4-1s,domain=open.spotify.com; ||adstudio-assets.scdn.co/*.mp3$media,…; media-us.amillionads.com/*.mp3$media,… (BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt 854-856), plus the open.spotify.com#⁠%#⁠ blank-MP4 ad-video proxy and spotify.com#⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('trusted-replace-fetch-response', …/audio/…). (shortened; the full text is in the run artifacts)

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reporter-defined target — the in-player 'Publicité' break panel with '1 sur 3', '60 s de pause restantes' and 'En savoir plus' — is Spotify's own advertising, served from Spotify's own first-party hosts. Filter policy document (AdguardTeam/KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md):⁠ "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules." The remaining ad break UI is not produced by a general filtering rule, so neither blocking it nor unblocking it is warranted. Not anti-adblock:⁠ no ad-blocker detection message or wall was observed (the 'Bloqué :⁠ 0' panel in the screenshot is AdGuard's own UI), so the anti-adblock rule path does not apply. The general part of the report (ads also not blocked on YouTube and game platforms) names no URL, page or element and is not actionable from this issue; only https:⁠//open.spotify.com/collection/tracks is reportable here.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"55fff5ae6ebcfc02855ec699e782e3a73a842036886e3c973ec65a65f5f1d81c"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reporter's annotated banner on oberpfalzdaheim.de is the publisher's own Black Friday subscription offer, served from the site's own asset API and rendered as an article media block whose click leads to the same publisher's OnetzPlus subscription page on onetz.de - i.e. first-party self-promotion, so per the run instruction's policy no rule is written and the report is recommended for closing.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ 'The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing.' The reporter-annotated banner advertises the publisher's own paid subscription. Filter policy document (AdGuard filter policy, 'Limitations and exceptions'):⁠ 'The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked', and its terminology defines self-promotion as 'the banners of a website promoting goods and services owned by the site owner, for which they do not receive compensation from third parties' - the banner's creative is first-party and its click target is the same publisher's own subscription-offers page, with no third-party advertiser involved. The instruction's other closing rules (paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, uncaptured anti-adblock detection) do not apply:⁠ the page shows no anti-adblock wall, popup or paywall, and the reporter's problem type is 'Ads'.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43723913646

The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The Lithuanian anti-adblock wall on go.lnk.lt's live player was not reproducible:⁠ the reported /live-tv page loads with no wall, and the reconstructed player page shows an unrelated "Nepavyksta paleisti turinio" error both with and without filtering. No detector script appears in the captured requests, so per the run instruction's anti-adblock rule the report goes to a maintainer instead of a generated rule.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction:⁠ 'Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer.' No detector script appears in the filtered HAR (artifact:⁠har:⁠36a46ded-fedb-4e9f-91da-272f20bf5bea) or the control HAR (artifact:⁠har:⁠e636236d-ca04-43cc-be43-73e6faabba6c). Run instruction:⁠ 'German anti-adblock walls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing' does not apply — the wall text in the reporter screenshot is Lithuanian ('Prašome išjungti reklamos blokavimą'), so this is an 'other' anti-adblock wall. The reported wall could not be reached for observation:⁠ the reported URL /live-tv shows no wall in either session, and the reconstructed player page fails with 'Nepavyksta paleisti turinio' both filtered and unfiltered, so no selector or request could be tied to the wall.

## Artifacts

Indeterminate — audioforum.si shows its cookie notice as a first-party Elementor popup (div#⁠elementor-popup-modal-38, class .elementor-popup-modal) that the reported filters do not hide; the fix fits the existing shared rule <⁠domains⁠>#⁠#⁠.elementor-popup-modal in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt, so audioforum.si should be added to it. ## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — socialbee.com's two reported overlays are Elementor Pro popups (a 20%-off email modal shown 5 s after load and a mobile "Try SocialBee for free / No card required" scroll bar), both matched by the Elementor popup wrapper class. Adding socialbee.com to the existing `.elementor-popup-modal` family in the Popups filter hid the reported modal in the CLI-proxy experiment, but one review verified it while the experiment refused the reveal-step check and two reviews kept counting a third-party Ada chat teaser as the symptom, so the rule is carried unverified.

## Candidate for review

`socialbee.com,thisonlineweb.com,howweelearn.com,blockerx.net,pocketwanderings.com,listoffreeware.com##.elementor-popup-modal`

AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt

Two other validation runs of the same candidate were rejected only because the review extended the symptom scope to a third-party Ada support-chat teaser (#⁠ada-intro-frame from static.ada.support) and to the inline first-party 'Try SocialBee for free' article button, neither of which is an Elementor popup and neither of which this rule targets.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — milx.app opens a large fixed lead-capture/subscribe panel ("Get Up to $10,000 in YouTube Monetization Advances" with e-mail, YouTube channel and comment fields) over the article once the reader scrolls past the third heading. Hiding the panel's own `.modal-subscribe` container verified clean in the before/after experiment:⁠ the overlay is gone, the article is readable and the page keeps its layout. ## Rule `milx.app##.modal-subscribe` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's policy list does not cover this report:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not an anti-adblock wall or scam page — it is a self-opening subscribe/lead-capture popup, which the AdGuard Popups filter is defined to block. The popup is a first-party overlay baked into the served HTML with no distinct request behind it, so a domain-scoped element-hiding rule is the appropriate, non-circumventing fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3b7ce90a9f581da50208330bd4750214849be8f8/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — manutd.one reserves 300px-tall ad card containers (`.nz-ad-card`, aria-label "Рекламный блок") whose ad requests are already blocked by the shipped lists, so the page shows large empty ad placeholders in the article column and one labelled "Реклама" that the reporter marked. Hiding them with the domain-scoped cosmetic rule `manutd.one##.nz-ad-card` was verified in the proxy-filtered browser:⁠ all empty slots gone, no remaining instances, page integrity intact, article content unchanged. ## Rule `manutd.one##.nz-ad-card` ## Policy rationale The reported elements are empty third-party ad containers (Google Ad Manager units / prebid SSP bids), not the site's own first-party advertising, so the 'first-party ads — no rule' policy line does not apply. Not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and no anti-adblock wall at all (antiAdblockDetected false in every phase), so no anti-adblock policy line applies. No rule of the run instruction closes this report; the leftover empty ad placeholders are a standard cosmetic target. ## Place in the list [CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3b7ce90a9f581da50208330bd4750214849be8f8/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43729423065 Automated analysis against filters at `3b7ce90`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On the reported page (www⁠.ign.com/news, mobile viewport, all of the reporter's lists active through the AdGuard CLI proxy) the reported privacy-consent modal never renders:⁠ the page loads fully, no overlay covers the content, and the site's OneTrust CMP itself reports ShowAlertNotice=false with all consent groups pre-enabled, while its container is already hidden by the existing generic rule #⁠#⁠#⁠onetrust-consent-sdk. No rule can be written or validated for an overlay that does not appear, so I recommend closing the report as not reproduced.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's policy lists no rule that blocks generation for cookie/consent-notice annoyances:⁠ it closes first-party ads, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls, and this report is none of those (it is a privacy-consent modal). The only captured overlay candidate is the OneTrust CMP, whose container is already covered by the existing generic element-hiding rule, so no new or extended rule is warranted. The recommended close rests on non-reproduction of the reported overlay on the successfully loaded page, not on a policy restriction.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"7a9d2fd3108f29e3fadae0b1abdbe55a638714851e8fcfdb230697651b3f02d3"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

With the reporter's filter lists, sporteurope.tv's match page shows "Datenschutz-Einstellungen nicht verfügbar ... Bitte deaktiviere ggf. deinen Adblocker" in the player, and once the site's consent wall is accepted the player shows "Adblocker erkannt — Bitte deaktiviere deinen Adblocker, um dieses Video abspielen zu können". The stream is withheld by the site's own German ad-blocker detection, which the run's policy gives no rule, so I recommend closing (the interim Cookie Notices block of the site's Usercentrics consent API is documented for a maintainer).

## Still visible after the rule

- Top of SC Rist Wedel vs. Baskets Juniors TSG Westerstede match page, video-player area behind the 'WEITER MIT WERBUNG, TRACKING UND COOKIES' consent wall — The live-stream/video player content is not available; the player region is occupied by a consent wall with 'AKZEPTIEREN UND WEITER', so the match stream is withheld. This is recorded as gated/missing video content, not as the consent dialog itself.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, filter policy:⁠ "German anti-adblock walls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing. This covers only a German site's wall or popup that detects the ad blocker and asks to disable it or to allowlist the site." The page itself shows such a wall:⁠ "Adblocker erkannt / Bitte deaktiviere deinen Adblocker, um dieses Video abspielen zu können, und lade die Seite neu" in the stream player, and in the reported state "Die Datenschutz-Einstellungen konnten nicht geladen werden. Bitte deaktiviere ggf. deinen Adblocker und lade die Seite neu". Both ask the visitor to disable the ad blocker and withhold the stream. Restoring playback would require neutralizing the detection (unblocking the IMA3/GTM/Facebook ad and tracking requests or defeating the detector), which the same policy gives no rule for. No rule is written for this report; a maintainer decides on closing it.

## Artifacts

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported blank band is present on lca.pl only in the desktop layout, as an empty reserved ad slot (ins.staticpubads89354 with a tiny 'Reklama' label) whose ad request is already blocked, and absent in the reporter's mobile viewport, so neither a reproducing rule nor a not-reproduced close is supportable. The repository already hides that slot wrapper for lca.pl in PolishFilter, and the trial hide left \~90 px of page-layout whitespace and was rejected by review, so this needs a maintainer's judgement.

## Still visible after the rule

- Below the weather forecast widget (Legnica, 7°C / 10°C / 10°C) and the yellow tag bar, immediately above the lead story image 'Ponad 2,4 mln zł na nową drogę rowerową w Legnicy' at the top of the page — Reserved empty advertising slot rendered as a wide blank white band (\~80-90 px tall) spanning the main content column between the weather box and the lead article. No ad creative, no visible 'Reklama' label, divider or frame is present in the band; only white page background is shown, so the space is still reserved but unused and the leading story is pushed down.
- Main content column, between the weather forecast row and the lead story image — Large blank white reserved advertising band roughly 90 px tall above the lead story. No ad creative is visible; this is the reporter-defined empty advertising slot/placeholder area.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The ruweb.net homepage shows a first-party cookie/personal-data consent banner inside a fixed full-viewport overlay `.policy-alert__wrapper`; the domain-scoped element-hiding rule `ruweb.net##.policy-alert__wrapper` was verified by the CLI baseline experiment to hide it with the page left intact. ## Rule `ruweb.net##.policy-alert__wrapper` ## Policy rationale The reported defect is a cookie/personal-data consent notice, which the repository's Annoyances/Cookie Notices filter explicitly covers (filter-policy.md, 'AdGuard Cookie Notices filter'). It is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page shows a consent notice, and the run instruction's German anti-adblock rule does not apply. No anti-adblock detector is involved, so the 'any other anti-adblock wall' gate does not apply either. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/3b7ce90a9f581da50208330bd4750214849be8f8/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"b4d43152ef15a0e6701a14d029e10038a3703501d84926869fbc082deb384af3"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The reported iQiyi anti-adblock black-screen could not be reproduced:⁠ the sports player refuses playback in this runner's region with its own \⁠"地域受限...【A00111】\⁠" overlay, so no ad-block-detection script ever ran and the captured requests show none. The run instruction requires that detector evidence before writing an anti-adblock rule, so the report goes to a maintainer to check in the CN region (note the reporter's configuration has no Annoyances filter, where iqiyi's existing anti-adblock rules live).

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, verbatim:⁠ "Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." The reported URL is neither a German site nor a scam/phishing page, so this clause governs the report. The captured requests do not show an ad-block-detection script producing the wall:⁠ the page never entered its ad/anti-adblock code path. The player refused playback with its own overlay "地域受限，去看看其他节目吧【A00111】" and no anti-adblock text exists anywhere in the DOM (checked '广告被拦截' and '关闭拦截插件':⁠ absent), so no detection request could be observed or pointed at. The symptom is therefore not reachable in this run (region-restricted player, no geographic proxy backend available), so no candidate rule could be evidence-backed or validated; the report needs a maintainer who can observe the CN-region player.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43742244594

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"feea5fefc7b6784630cc70f073fe9c67b831155bd588bd91e46bce921926585a"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported grok.com defect is a first-party "Get 50% off Premium" upsell toast that the reporter only sees after signing in; the anonymous page I could load renders no such element (no "upsell" class anywhere, no "50% off"/"Claim offer" text in the DOM), so no selector could be validated. The repository already has a grok.com self-promo rule for this element family in AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt, so the fix likely belongs there but needs a maintainer with a signed-in session.

## Candidate for review

`grok.com##div[role="button"][class*="upsell-small"]`

AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt

Not verified: The target toast only renders in the signed-in grok.com app, which this run cannot reach (sign-in is a refused unsafe control). On the reported URL the anonymous page renders no upsell element at all:⁠ apply_rule ended with baseline_symptom_absent / unmatchedBaselineSelector 'div[⁠role="button"]⁠[⁠class*="upsell-small"]⁠', so no phase and no visual review judged the rule. The selector is derived from the repository's existing grok.com self-promo rule (self-promo.txt:⁠1307, class prefix 'upsell-small relative sm:⁠fixed') rather than from observed live markup. A maintainer should confirm the class in a signed-in session before adding it, or simply update the existing rule in the same file.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43745246144

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://socialxup.com/shuheikanaiwa](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fsocialxup.com%2Fshuheikanaiwa) ### Comment > On socialxup.com, links do not respond while AdGuard is enabled. For example, on https://socialxup.com/shuheikanaiwa, tapping the "SocialXup" logo in the header does nothing, and many other links on the site do not respond either. Everything works normally when AdGuard is disabled. > > This started after these socialxup.com rules were added to the AdGuard Japanese filter: > socialxup.com##+js(addEventListener-defuser, click, [native code]) > socialxup.com##:not(a):matches-css(cursor:pointer):xpath(div[not(ancestor::a)]) > > The first rule seems to block the site's own click handling (React's click listeners are bound functions, so they stringify as "[native code]"). Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — gzt.com articles show empty 'REKLAM'-labelled ad placeholders (the strip the reporter circled plus repeats further down) because the Google ad tag is already blocked by the Base filter. A domain-scoped hide of the ad unit, gzt.com#⁠#⁠aside:⁠has(⁠> .banner-ad-rule), removed all seven units in validation, but the vision review kept rejecting it only because the related-news band (content-visibility:⁠auto content, not painted in the capture) reads as reserved ad space, so the rule is handed over unverified.

## Candidate for review

`gzt.com##aside:has(> .banner-ad-rule)`

TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: environmentExperiment was inconclusive in all three runs though its own probe saw the 7 ad units visible before and hidden after (heights 31-36px -⁠> 0, adElementStatus phaseB visible / phaseC hidden). The visual review's rejection rests solely on blank bands under 'İlginizi Çekebilir':⁠ those are .stack-layout ⁠> .feed-section-layout content sections (1159-1236px, content-visibility:⁠auto, zero .banner-ad-rule units, article.feed-card stories with blocked/unloaded thumbnails) that Chromium does not paint offscreen in a full-page capture, so they were read as residual reserved ad height. pageIntegrity was intact and observedDamage empty in every run, and DOM checks measured the ad units before [⁠31,36,36,31,31,31,31]⁠ and after [⁠0,0,0,0,0,0,0]⁠. A dependency-free equivalent verified in the DOM is aside[⁠aria-label="Reklam"]⁠, matching the same 7 units and excluding the 'İlginizi Çekebilir' aside.

## Still visible after the rule

- Document y=5216..6028 — further blank continuation of the reserved block — The tile remains entirely blank white reserved space; the empty advertising/recommendation block continues with no creative or content loaded.
- Document y=6520..7332 (tile 11); the same continuous blank region extends across supplied tiles 10–12, y=5868..7984 — Large continuous blank reserved advertising area with no ad creative, no visible 'REKLAM' label, frame, or placeholder block. The reserved ad height remains after the candidate; it is not ordinary section spacing and is recorded as a residual empty-ad footprint.
- Document y=7824..8636 — Full tile is blank white reserved space:⁠ no ad creative, no visible 'Reklam'/REKLAM label, no frame or divider and no article content — only an empty advertising-sized gap between the page's content blocks.
- Document y=8476..9288 — Continuous blank white reserved space filling the tile:⁠ no creative, no ad label, frame or placeholder block, and no page content — a further empty ad-sized gap in the lower part of the article.
- Document y=9128..9940 — Tile remains entirely blank white reserved space with no ad creative, no 'Reklam' label, frame or divider — the empty advertising area continues lower down the page.
- and 1 more of the same, in the run artifacts

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On cleanip.io/who-am-i two fixed `
` rails hold 广告-labelled ad cards for proxy vendors (B2proxy, 环球VPN, 易联, X-SPARK, USVPS24) plus an "广告位招商" ad-slot card, and they still render with the repo filters. Adding `cleanip.io##aside.mpswa-rail` to the site's existing group in ChineseFilter/sections/specific.txt hid both rails in A/B/C validation (target 2 visible → 0, page integrity intact, no residue). ## Rule `cleanip.io##aside.mpswa-rail` ## Policy rationale The run instruction closes first-party ads, paywalls and German anti-adblock walls. None applies:⁠ the page shows two ad rails explicitly labelled 广告 whose inventory is offered for sale to third parties (a house "广告位招商" = ad-space-for-rent card sits in each rail) and whose cards promote external proxy vendors (B2proxy, 环球VPN / 台湾纯净校园网 IP, 易联, X-SPARK, USVPS24) — compensated third-party advertising, not the site owner's own self-promotion as the filter policy defines it. The repository already filters this site's ad surfaces (`cleanip.io##div[aria-label^="Sponsored"]`, `cleanip.io##div[aria-label="赞助内容"]`, `cleanip.io##.iu--banner`, `cleanip.io##.nf-campaign`, `cleanip.io##.netfish-invite-compact`), so cleanip.io advertising is in scope; the new rule only adds the rail container the existing rules do not cover. No anti-adblock gate, paywall or scam page is involved, so the anti-adblock and dangerous-page clauses of the policy do not apply. ## Place in the list [ChineseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/37437333d310bf2e516933d3d3750acd40d77932/ChineseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 63](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/37437333d310bf2e516933d3d3750acd40d77932/ChineseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L63). ## Screenshots
